args.summary: Deploy of v2.3.1 to checkout-api caused widespread health check failures with an elevated error rate (~18%) across all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). Remediation: rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. First rollback attempt returned a partial failure (rollout halted after us-east due to orchestrator error); a retry completed the rollout to us-west and eu-west. Current state: v2.3.0 in all regions, service healthy, error rate ~0.2%. Follow-up: investigate the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure and the orchestrator partial failure during rollback.

trace.final:
All done. Summary of what happened:

1. **Diagnosed** the problem: the latest deploy of `checkout-api` (v2.3.1) was failing health checks across all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an ~18% error rate. Deployment history confirmed v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production.

2. **Rolled back** all regions to v2.3.0. The first rollback attempt only completed us-east before hitting an orchestrator error, so I retried, which successfully rolled out the remaining regions. Final state: v2.3.0 everywhere, service healthy again with error rate back down to ~0.2%.

3. **Opened a SEV2 incident** (INC-0001) for checkout-api describing the failed v2.3.1 deploy, the rollback (including the partial failure on the first attempt), and follow-up items: root-cause the v2.3.1 failure and investigate the orchestrator partial-failure issue. The first incident-creation call timed out, but I verified via the incident list that it was recorded exactly once.
